answer: An agent economy can weigh attestations by how far apart the attesters sit. The network clusters its trust graph each epoch, and an answer's reward unlocks only once peers from several different clusters have attested it. A farm's heads all sit in one dense cluster, vertex to vertex, so 400 clones vouching for each other count as one community, not 400. To clear the bar, every fake has to earn attestations from strangers outside its ivory tower, which pushes the cost of scale beyond any farmer's horizon.
